title: A₄ Has No Subgroup of Order 6 — A 0-Axiom Structural Proof
problemStatement: The parent entry (lagrange-theorem-oq-03) proves the A₄ counterexample to the converse of Lagrange's theorem but discharges its arithmetic atoms (|A₄| = 12 and a count of squares) with `native_decide`, which depends on the `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom. Prove that A₄ has no subgroup of order 6 fully structurally — zero axioms beyond the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound, never enumerating group elements.

insights: Index 2 is the single structural lever: a subgroup of index 2 is normal with an order-2 quotient, so g² ∈ H for every g — no element enumeration needed.
Every 3-cycle is a square: order 3 gives σ = σ⁴ = (σ²)², so the 'all squares inside' property of an index-2 subgroup drags every 3-cycle into H.
Generation closes the argument: since the 3-cycles generate A₄ (`closure_three_cycles_eq_alternating`), an order-6 subgroup containing them all would be the whole group, contradicting |H| = 6.
|A₄| = 12 is obtained from `card_alternatingGroup` (n!/2) closed by kernel `decide`, which adds no axioms — the key difference from the parent's `native_decide`/`Lean.ofReduceBool` route.

Cardinality transport across the injective inclusion A₄ ↪ Perm(Fin 4) via `equivMapOfInjective` lets the whole argument live one level up among permutations while the contradiction is read off downstairs.
builtItems: a4_card: Fintype.card (alternatingGroup (Fin 4)) = 12 via card_alternatingGroup + kernel decide (LagrangeTheoremOQ03OQ02.lean:49)
sq_mem_of_index_two: index-2 normal subgroup contains every square (LagrangeTheoremOQ03OQ02.lean:55)
index_two_of_card_six: an order-6 subgroup of A₄ has index 2 (LagrangeTheoremOQ03OQ02.lean:66)
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has the A₄ counterexample only implicitly; there is no off-the-shelf lemma 'A₄ has no subgroup of order 6', so the generation-based argument is assembled here from card_alternatingGroup, closure_three_cycles_eq_alternating, and normal_of_index_eq_two.
nextSteps: Generalize the 'index 2 ⟹ all squares ⟹ generators inside' template to other forbidden subgroup orders in larger alternating groups.
Assemble the full subgroup-order spectrum of A₄ (only 1, 2, 3, 4, 12 are realized) structurally from the same generation and Sylow ingredients.
